prompts.note: D1 floor 3% (code default) + 1c/D7 long-gap rule, options agents
prompts.old: 5% of current account equity in option premium (limit price x contracts x 100), rounded to whole contracts, and never above the max-position limit; it must also fit remaining max-deployed, max-open-position and daily-loss capacity. If one contract alone exceeds the max-position limit, or remaining capacity is below 5%, skip the entry and report the reason. Account limits, not AlphaDesk, govern size. AlphaDesk-guarded openings are limited to 10 contracts per order. If your minimum entry would need more than 10 contracts, prefer an eligible contract inside your delta and expiry rules whose 10 contracts meet it; if none does, enter 10 contracts, which is below the standard size and acceptable. Never split one intent into several orders.
prompts.new:
3% of current account equity in option premium (limit price x contracts x 100), rounded to whole contracts, and never above the max-position limit; it must also fit remaining max-deployed, max-open-position and daily-loss capacity. If one contract alone exceeds the max-position limit, or remaining capacity is below 3%, skip the entry and report the reason. Account limits, not AlphaDesk, govern size. AlphaDesk-guarded openings are limited to 10 contracts per order. If your minimum entry would need more than 10 contracts, prefer an eligible contract inside your delta and expiry rules whose 10 contracts meet it; if none does, enter 10 contracts, which is below the standard size and acceptable. Never split one intent into several orders.
- Long gaps (new openings only, never a reason to sell): a long gap follows this session when the next regular session opens more than 24 hours after this session closes (a weekend or a market holiday); during the regular session compare broker_clock.next_open with session_close_utc, both from prophet_get_datetime. In a session before a long gap: open no new single-leg option once minutes_to_close is 120 or less; and before then, open a single-leg option only if the cost of the single-leg options you hold in that direction, plus the unfilled quantity of your working, planned or submission-uncertain single-leg openings in that direction, plus the candidate, stays within 10% of current account equity (held: remaining quantity x broker average entry premium x 100; unfilled openings and the candidate: quantity x limit x 100; bullish means calls and bearish means puts, never netted). Count each intent once: the filled part of a partly filled or retried opening is held cost, only its unfilled part is reserved, and the candidate is never added twice. If session_close_utc or broker_clock.next_open is unavailable, treat the session as one before a long gap and record which time was missing. Debit verticals are exempt from this rule but not from any other limit. A position above this limit is never sold because of it, and this rule never delays an exit.

prompts.old: Re-read the exact contract quote immediately before the guarded order and submit at once (aim for under 90 seconds); OP2 rejects quote evidence older than 2 minutes and that check still decides. Write your logs after the order call. Review an unfilled opening order at the second heartbeat after submission: re-check the setup and fills, and cancel it unless it still qualifies at the same limit. Copy order IDs exactly from the latest get_orders result; never retype them. Before any replacement, confirm the cancel is terminal and read its cumulative filled quantity; a replacement covers only the verified remaining quantity, never more. When your recorded exit plan still requires a position to close: after the cancel is terminal, reconcile fills, the held quantity and any other working exits, then submit a freshly priced replacement for the remaining unreserved quantity, preferably in the same heartbeat. If the cancel, fills, position or quote is uncertain, do not submit a duplicate exit; record the block with prophet_log_decision and continue at the next heartbeat. The second-heartbeat review above applies to opening orders only.

- Option quotes: take the bid, ask, sizes and quote time of an option contract, a candidate or one you hold, from prophet_get_options_chain for its exact expiry and type. A position read (prophet_get_options_position) gives exposure and a mark, not an executable quote, and it reports not found for a contract you do not hold; prophet_get_quote is for stocks and ETFs and fails on an option symbol. When the chain does not return a usable quote for a contract you hold, read that exact contract once with prophet_get_options_quote (held contracts only, read-only): it returns the bid, ask, sizes and quote time with the same indicative quality, or says why it cannot. It is a quote, never a mark, and if it also has no fresh quote the existing no-quote rules apply.

prompts.note: 1b Prophet config: measurable swing-only rules pointing at Trading Guidance
prompts.old:
mainly with long calls; use long puts only for clearly bearish setups, never as hedges. Trade swings only (a paper-trading trial): open no new same-session scalps.
- Choose an expiration beyond the intended hold, 21 to 45 calendar days out, with a delta magnitude of about 0.6 to 0.7.
- Require a daily breakout aligned with the weekly trend.
- Enter after a completed-bar retest holds the broken level and momentum resumes; do not assume a close-price fill.
- Skip conflicting timeframes and choppy action.
- Exit when the retest fails or the higher-timeframe trend breaks.
prompts.new:
with swing trades only, mainly with long calls; use long puts only for clearly bearish setups, never as hedges.
- Choose an expiration beyond the intended hold, inside the swing expiry window and delta range in Trading Guidance.
- Trade with the trend: a call needs the call trend condition and a put the put trend condition in Trading Guidance.
- Require a daily breakout within the last 5 completed sessions, measured against the breakout level in Trading Guidance.
- Enter only after a completed daily retest holds the broken level and the entry trigger in Trading Guidance is met; do not assume a close-price fill.
- Exit on a failed retest or a broken trend, both as defined in Trading Guidance.

prompts.note: 1b Prophet guidance: swing-only expiry window and the numeric trend/breakout/retest/trigger/exit definitions
prompts.old:
Label each position a scalp or a swing at entry and keep that horizon. Choose an expiry beyond your intended hold, limited to what AlphaDesk accepts: AlphaDesk only passes an option that expires 1 to 180 calendar days out, so a contract outside that window cannot pass and is not a candidate. Expiry windows AlphaDesk accepts (your Strategy Rules decide which styles you may open): scalp (exit in the same session): 2 to 10 calendar days to expiry (OP2 blocks same-day expiry); swing: 21 to 60 calendar days to expiry. Use a delta magnitude of about 0.4 to 0.7 (a put's delta is negative, so compare its absolute value). Pick the expiry first with prophet_get_option_expirations using a min_dte and max_dte inside that window (choose only a confirmed date; dates it lists as unchecked are unknown, not absent; it lists dates with listed call contracts, so confirm a put chain exists before proposing a put), then call prophet_get_options_chain with that expiration and the matching type. Use max_cost only as a ceiling on ONE contract, never as a position budget.
- Your Strategy Rules decide every entry and exit (a breakout aligned with the higher timeframe, a completed-bar retest that holds, momentum resuming). Trading Guidance adds no further gate; use the option cost discipline line below. For scalps use completed intraday bars (complete=true only) and record the bar timeframe; for swings use completed daily bars and the weekly trend.
prompts.new:
Choose an expiry beyond your intended hold, limited to what AlphaDesk accepts: AlphaDesk only passes an option that expires 1 to 180 calendar days out, so a contract outside that window cannot pass and is not a candidate. Your swing expiry window: 21 to 60 calendar days to expiry. Use a delta magnitude of about 0.4 to 0.7 (a put's delta is negative, so compare its absolute value). Pick the expiry first with prophet_get_option_expirations using a min_dte and max_dte inside that window (choose only a confirmed date; dates it lists as unchecked are unknown, not absent; it lists dates with listed call contracts, so confirm a put chain exists before proposing a put), then call prophet_get_options_chain with that expiration and the matching type. Use max_cost only as a ceiling on ONE contract, never as a position budget.
- Your Strategy Rules decide every entry and exit; the definitions below give their numbers. Use completed daily bars only (complete=true).
- Trend (the stand-in for the higher timeframe): for a call, the last completed daily close is above its 20-day average and the 5-session change of that average is 0% or higher; for a put, the close is below its 20-day average and that change is 0% or lower. get_daily_features gives the average, the close versus the average and the 5-session change; name the figures you used.
- Breakout level: for a call, the highest high of the 20 completed sessions before the breakout bar; for a put, the lowest low of those 20 sessions. The breakout bar is a completed daily bar that closed above that level (call) or below it (put), within the last 5 completed sessions. get_daily_features measures high_prior_20_sessions and low_prior_20_sessions over the 20 sessions before the LATEST completed bar, so they equal the breakout level only when the latest bar is the breakout bar. For a breakout one to four sessions ago, read that symbol's completed daily bars with prophet_get_historical_bars (timeframe 1Day, about 30 sessions, complete=true bars only; state the feed) and take the level from the 20 sessions before the breakout bar. Record the level, the breakout date and the feed in your WATCHLIST record after the close and reuse that record later; never estimate the level.
- Retest: after the breakout bar, a completed daily bar came back near the level: for a call its low is within -0.5% to +2% of the breakout level ((low / level - 1) x 100 from -0.5 to 2); for a put its high is within -2% to +0.5% of it ((high / level - 1) x 100 from -2 to 0.5). No completed daily close since the breakout bar may be back through the level (below it for a call, above it for a put).
- Entry trigger: the latest completed daily close is above the previous session's high (call) or below the previous session's low (put), and that close is no more than 4% beyond the breakout level. Enter at a later permitted regular-session evaluation; do not assume a close-price fill.
- Failed retest: a completed daily close back through the breakout level (below it for a call, above it for a put). Broken trend: a completed daily close on the wrong side of the 20-day average (below it for a call, above it for a put).

prompts.note: 1b Prophet: daily-bar operating rule instead of the intraday batch-scan rule
prompts.old: Your setups can trigger during the session. On every regular-session heartbeat: reconcile, then work through your strategy universe in batches (about 15 names per beat), using only completed bars (complete=true) in the timeframe your Strategy Rules require for each condition: completed daily bars where your rules say so, and completed 5-minute bars only for intraday entries your rules allow, and re-price earlier candidates whose option evidence is older than one beat. If the scan is incomplete, record where you stopped with prophet_log_decision (action WATCHLIST, "scan cursor") and continue from there next beat; incomplete research is never a reason to stop scanning. After the close, record next-session ideas with action WATCHLIST (symbol, trigger level, invalidation, expiry window). For every candidate that you rejected, record the single number that failed
prompts.new: Daily-bar facts only change after each close. Scan the strategy universe on completed daily bars after the close or before the open (record next-session candidates with `prophet_log_decision`, action "WATCHLIST": symbol, trigger level, invalidation, expiry window), then during the session act on WATCHLIST triggers, refresh exact option evidence, and manage positions; do not re-fetch unchanged daily history every beat. When you are flat, nothing is pending and you hold no WATCHLIST candidate, do not poll bars that are still forming (they cannot satisfy a completed-bar rule): reconcile, record the outcome and end the beat. For every symbol that cleared a recent high or looked like a candidate but was rejected, record the single number that failed (for example its volume ratio, extension or average slope)
